propositions: A duplicate-closed child with a live replacement link is exempt from producing a completion-verifier attestation by the close gate (transition_close.py:253-260), but the certification path (llm/completion.py:170-199) requires such an attestation on every closed child, creating an uncertifiable parent with no non-deceptive remedy.

The close and certification gates employ inconsistent logic: the close gate exempts disposition-class bugs (duplicate, not_a_bug, escalated) with live replacement links from verification; the certification gate ignores this exemption and treats unsigned closure as uncertified, withholding the parent's signature.

A disposition-closed child cannot earn an attestation through honest means: reopening and re-closing follows the same exemption branch, and deleting the replacement link is the only way to certify but requires misrepresenting the ticket.

The completion-verifier attestation for a disposition close must carry manifest text reading 'DISPOSITION <class>' and the replacement ticket id, not a false 'PASS' verdict, to maintain auditable distinction between verified completions and bookkeeping dispositions.
A force-close guard positioned before the disposition branch prevents --force-close from bypassing verification by obtaining a disposition attestation, and this ordering is semantically load-bearing.
